content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently working with the [product_name] Web Editor. It's an impressive tool, but I notice some unresolved issues. I'm transferring the TD interface to the Web Editor and most functions are working well. However, I'm facing a challenge with the weekly time scheduler. The 7-day checkbox operates correctly and the [product_name] reflects this. But I can't get the three start and end time schedulers to function properly; while they work fine on the TD interface, the numbers shown on the [product_name] Web Editor in the browser are odd. I've tried using analog and scaled time—still can't get it right. Could someone provide a simple example to view and SET the three scheduler times? Thanks a lot

Here's the issue: The switching times of a weekly timer are BCD coded. For a readable display in the extended Web Editor, you need to set the analog input/output field to HEX format. However, a '16 #' label for hexadecimal also appears in these fields. Additionally, hours and minutes must be separated. For example: - Start time at 8:00 am: displayed as 16#8 and 16#0 - End time at 10:00 pm: displayed as 16#22 and 16#0 Please refer to the attachment.
That's not the most user-friendly solution, since clients may get confused by those numbers. If you want users to set a new time, does it mean you need two additional analog inputs?

Whether ideal or not, it's currently the only way to achieve this. When changing the value, you don't need to type '16#'; that's only shown for display purposes. I'll make a screen video for you later.

Thank you for the video. I now understand how the timers are displayed. I'm going to start adding all the timers. Here's a snapshot of the irrigation map for a large home using the [product_name] Web Editor.

Hello [user_name] (and everyone), I've found a workaround for this problem. Take a look at this topic: How to remove the hex label (16#) when showing switch times for a weekly timer in the extended web server?

analysis.insight_summary: Users value the strong functionality and versatility of the [product_name] Web Editor, especially for managing weekly timers. However, challenges arise with usability—viewing and setting multiple scheduler times is unclear due to non-intuitive BCD-coded and hexadecimal time displays. The requirement to use hexadecimal format (including the '16#' label) introduces confusion, making it difficult for end clients to input or interpret timer settings, and reducing overall accessibility.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek a straightforward, intuitive way to display and set multiple timer start/end times within the Web Editor—similar to the previous TD interface. They prefer solutions that hide technical formatting and eliminate the need for clients to interpret hexadecimal codes, aiming for a user-friendly experience for both viewing and editing timer settings.
